blind_target.authors: Diener, E., Tay, L., & Myers, D. G.
blind_target.title: The religion paradox: If religion makes people happy, why are so many dropping out?
blind_target.evidence_quote: Study 1 was a direct replication of previous cross-cultural research on the religiosity- adjustment relation. Yet, this study differed from previous research in three important ways. First, previous research operationalized psychological adjustment as life satisfaction (Stavrova et al., 2013), subjective well-being (Diener et al., 2011), depression (Leurent et al., 2013), or social self-esteem (Gebauer et al., 2012b).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our results fully and firmly replicated and extended prior evidence for cross-cultural differences in religious adjustment benefits.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The reported moderation agrees with the prior positive moderation findings.

prior_decision.quote: Yet, this study differed from previous research in three important ways. First, previous research operationalized psychological adjustment as life satisfaction (Stavrova et al., 2013), subjective well-being (Diener et al., 2011), depression (Leurent et al., 2013), or social self-esteem (Gebauer et al., 2012b). From an RASV perspective, however, global self-esteem is the most appropriate adjustment indicator.
prior_decision.reason: Parent source inspection cannot establish that this is background only: the paper explicitly re-tests cross-cultural moderation with a changed adjustment measure. Measure differences alone do not rule out a conceptual replication. The two allowed Argon calls are exhausted; this proposed target remains unverified rather than being excluded on this quotation.

shipped_originals.title_o: Firm's resilience to supply chain disruptions: Scale development and empirical examination

blind_target.evidence_quote: The purpose is to replicate and extend Ambulkar et al.’s (2015) work testing resource reconfiguration as a mediator of the supply chain disruption/firm resilience relationship and testing risk management infrastructure as a moderator.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Two of four of Ambulkars et al.’s (2015) hypotheses were confirmed as relevant to firm resilience during the pandemic while two were not confirmed.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit partial confirmation of the four hypotheses from a single original paper. Original reference citation is unavailable in abstract.
